evidence.note: Entered plan mode, surveyed tests to enumerate required features, wrote a compiler_design.md plan file, and produced a 'comprehensive implementation plan' with a clear pass structure — a genuine feature roadmap in dependency order.

Implementation was big-bang: a single delegated agent wrote ALL modules (lexer, preprocessor, ast, parser, type_checker, codegen, main) at once, rather than staging incremental feature milestones each with an explicit done-check.

Long reactive loop — fixes failing tests in roughly numeric file order (00051, 00063, 00107, 00121, 00162, 00197, 00200, 00207...), each followed by a full suite rerun. Ordering follows test numbers, not a dependency-aware milestone plan that targets features unlocking the most tests.
After reaching 100% on c_testsuite (146 tests), deliberately shifted focus to wacc failures — a coarse, data-driven milestone transition loosely tied to test subsets.
Tracked progress at the aggregate level (611/780, 78.3%) as the effective done-signal, rather than per-feature completion criteria.

reasoning: The agent has a clear pass structure and a written feature roadmap in reasonable dependency order, and progress is genuinely tied to getting tests passing, with a coarse milestone shift from c_testsuite to wacc (anchor 5). It falls short of anchor 8 because the compiler was built big-bang rather than staged as fine-grained, dependency-sequenced feature milestones, and the subsequent work proceeds reactively in numeric test order with no per-feature test-subset done-signals defined in advance.
